record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Zauner’s conjecture for SIC fiducial vectors
record.original_question: Let the Clifford group be the normalizer of the Heisenberg group in the d-dimensional unitary group, and let z be the Clifford element acting on Weyl operators by z w(p,q) z* = w(q - p, -p). In every dimension d, can a Heisenberg-group fiducial vector for a covariant SIC-POVM be found among the eigenvectors of z?

evidence.quote:
The normalizer of the Heisenberg group within the unitaries U(d) is called the Clifford group. There exists an element z of the Clifford group which is defined via its action on the Weyl operators as
z w(p, q)z∗ = w(q − p, −p).
Zauner’s conjecture, as formulated in [3], runs: in any dimension d, a fiducial vector can be found among the eigenvectors of Z.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer d ≥ 2 and work in the Hilbert space ℂ^d. For p, q ∈ ℤ/dℤ, define the Weyl (displacement) operators w(p,q) on ℂ^d by
  w(p,q) |k⟩ = ω^{q(k+p/2)} |k+p⟩,
where ω = exp(2πi/d) (with the half-integer exponent interpreted via a 2d-th root of unity when d is odd, or via the standard projective convention when d is even). The Heisenberg–Weyl group H(d) is the group generated by the w(p,q) together with phases, and the Clifford group is its normalizer in the unitary group U(d).

There exists a Clifford-group element z whose action on Weyl operators is
  z w(p,q) z* = w(q − p, −p).

A unit vector φ ∈ ℂ^d is called a Heisenberg-covariant fiducial vector for a symmetric informationally complete POVM (SIC-POVM) if the d² rank-one projectors
  {(1/d) w(p,q) |φ⟩⟨φ| w(p,q)* : (p,q) ∈ (ℤ/dℤ)²}
form a SIC-POVM, equivalently
  |⟨φ | w(p,q) | φ⟩|² = 1/(d+1)   for all (p,q) ≠ (0,0).

Question: Is it true that for every dimension d ≥ 2 there exists a Heisenberg-covariant SIC fiducial vector φ that is an eigenvector of z?
artifact.status_search_result: Zauner's conjecture remains open in general. SIC fiducial vectors that are eigenvectors of the Zauner unitary have been constructed (numerically or exactly) in many specific dimensions, and a 2025 conditional construction via the Stark conjectures provides candidate fiducials in broad families of dimensions, but no unconditional proof for all d is known.

status_evidence.title: SIC POVMs and Zauner's Conjecture – Open Quantum Problems
status_evidence.snippet: The existence of SIC-POVMs in arbitrary finite dimensions remains an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Zauner's conjecture is still open in general.

status_evidence.title: A Constructive Approach to Zauner's Conjecture via the Stark Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Construction gives a valid SIC assuming the abelian Stark conjecture and a Shintani-Faddeev identity.
status_evidence.claim: A conditional construction exists, but unconditional proof is not yet available.
